 Live .  10,238 viewing 10238 viewing Head out as Rabada runs through Australia for rampant South Africa
 Tue 27 Oct 2026 - Sat 31 Oct 2026 , Men's International Test Match Series - 3rd Test - Day 5 of 5 South Africa vs Australia (batting), in play South Africa South Africa In Play Australia Australia 329 all out ( 82.3 ) 387 all out ( 134.4 ) 429 all out ( 125.1 ) 30 -3 ( 11.1 ) Australia require 258 runs to win with 7 wickets remaining South Africa innings: 329 all out from 82.3 overs
 387 all out from 134.4 overs
 Australia innings: 429 all out from 125.1 overs
 30 for 3 from 11.1 overs, in play
 What does history suggest could happen in Cape Town classic? 
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Australia need 288 to win third Test and series, SA need 10 wickets
 Rabada has Renshaw caught down leg side and Labschagne lbw in first over
 Head (14) also caught at fourth slip - Rabada's 350th Test wicket
 What does history suggest could happen? 
 Third Test, day five, Cape Town
 Close form Have your say on South Africa v Australia
 Get involved Live Reporting
 By Marc Higginson
 Aus 30-3 published at 11 overs 11 overs 
 South Africa are doing most things right this morning. I say most... between overs they're playing M People.
 A couple of singles keep Australia ticking along, albeit at a snail-like pace.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 09:20 GMT 09:20 GMT 
 Use the form on this page 
 To Phil (9.07) I agree with Rabada being underrated but would argue it's more than 'slightly'. His 350 wickets have come in only 75 Tests and at a strike-rate of under 40. The only reason he's not at 500 wickets is because South Africa don't play enough Test cricket.
 Will, London 
 63 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 28-3 published at 10 overs 10 overs 
 Cape Town looks a picture; Table Mountain bearing down on Newlands. Such is South Africa's dominance, they too feel overbearing for those of an Australian persuasion.
 Wiaan Mulder, bowling brisk medium pace, has the keeper up, some close catchers in and the Aussies are suffocating. It's a different challenge to the world-class fast bowling provided by Rabada but it's just as effective at the moment. Maiden.
 25 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 28-3 published at 9 overs 9 overs 
 The way this is going, the new batter Josh Inglis will get to watch his beloved Coventry City at 3pm today. Rabada is being clapped to the crease by the crowd and he concedes just a couple of singles in his latest over.
 54 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:11 GMT 09:11 GMT 
 KG Rabada's first four overs this morning. Relentless...
 Image source, CricViz 
 42 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 26-3 published at 8 overs 8 overs 
 I agree with that, Phil. He always touches 90mph, rarely errs on line and can move it both ways. A generational talent.
 The imposing Cameron Green gets his first boundary with a punch through the off side off Wiaan Mulder. Between deliveries, Green pauses and exhales. He knows what is riding on this.
 59 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 09:07 GMT 09:07 GMT 
 Use the form on this page 
 Image source, Getty Images I feel like Rabada is slightly under-rated in the grand scheme of things. 350 Test wickets at an average of 22 is outrageous. He's one of the greatest bowlers of the modern era.
 Phil, London 
 430 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 7 overs 7 overs 
 Head c Jansen b Rabada 14 (Aus 22-3) 
 Image source, Getty Images And another. Australia's key man is back in the sheds.
 Rabada probes that off-stump line, Head takes the bait and Marco Jansen gobbles up the catch at fourth slip.
 That's Rabada's 350th Test wicket. Only Dale Steyn has reached the landmark faster for the Proteas.
 537 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 09:01 GMT 09:01 GMT 
 Image source, CricViz South Africa to Travis Head so far...
 When it's wide, he scores. When it's straight, less so.
 26 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:00 GMT 09:00 GMT 
 Here's a reminder of what Australia are up against. They've done similar before, mind...
 5 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 17-2 published at 6 overs 6 overs 
 South Africa are making Australia work for every run. Aiden Markram makes a good stop at backward point, shortly after Head fends another off his moustache. Just two leg-byes in the over. 
 40 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:56 GMT 08:56 GMT 
 Graeme Smith 
Former South Africa captain on Sky Sports 
 Rabada looks a different man from the first innings when he wasn't well.
 82 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 15-2 published at 5 overs 5 overs 
 KG. Stop it!
 Rabada bowls a beauty which shapes away from Travis Head and leaves the left-hander swinging his bat like a rusty gate. The Rolls Royce is locked in, says Graeme Smith.
 Head just smiles then legs it to the other end the moment he gets the chance to nick a single. Though it does mean he keeps the strike to Marco Jansen.
 47 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 14-2 published at 4 overs 4 overs 
 Jansen continues with the shorter stuff to Green but the Australian number four is more secure after that scare earlier in the over. Maiden.
 19 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 14-2 published at 3.1 overs 3.1 overs 
 Cameron Green should put the lottery on. Marco Jansen gets one to rear up mamba-like and a leaden-footed Green fends it off and the ball almost drops on to his own stumps.
 20 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 14-2 published at 3 overs 3 overs 
 Rabada is running in hard here, getting nice shape and testing the technique of the batters. Cameron Green is the new batter and he is off the mark with a single through point.
 21 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 08:43 GMT 08:43 GMT 
 Have your say using the Get Involved button on this page 
 Feel for Labuschange here - seems fidgety and uncertain, similar to how Pope was in the Ashes before he was dropped. Needs taking out of the spotlight to work on his technique and approach.
 J, London 
 69 238 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 13-2 published at 2 overs 2 overs 
 Target 288 
 What I enjoyed most about that opening over - apart from Marnus being pinned lbw - was how Graeme Smith, one of the best captains in Test history, was wondering out loud why Rabada was bowling round the wicket to Renshaw. Cricket never follows a logical pattern.
 Travis Head gets off the mark with a beautiful driven four before slashing at the final ball of Marco Jansen's over to edge four more over gully's head.
 52 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 08:39 GMT 08:39 GMT 
 Image source, CricViz 
 134 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 WICKET published at 1 over 1 over 
 Labuschagne lbw b Rabada 4 (Aus 5-2) 
 Cape Town is rocking now. Marnus Labuschagne, who has got under the skin of the South Africans in this series, has to walk. He didn't last long and the four he did get was fourtunate. KG has Australia 5-2.
